plans.note: Sec 21.1 caps both Parties at one month of Fees paid 'without exception', which conflicts with the Excluded Claims regime in 21.2/21.3 and is far below a meaningful cap — likely material deviation. Read 21.2-21.4 together for carve-outs and supercap analysis.

Section 20 contains only a broad Customer-gives indemnity (20.1) with no Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity; Sec 9.3 cross-references a Section 20.5 that does not appear. Check whether Vendor indemnity is truly absent and whether the Customer indemnity is unacceptably broad.
Sec 12.4 imposes a 24-month, worldwide, all-product non-compete on Customer — presence trigger. Note the direct conflict with Sec 12.3, which disclaims any non-compete.
Sec 2.2 (first of two 2.2s) makes Vendor sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics — presence trigger; Sec 12.3 disclaims exclusivity, so flag the conflict.
No MFN obligation on Customer appears; Sec 12.3 expressly disclaims any most-favoured-customer commitment, which favours us. Confirm nothing in pricing (7.1, 8.3) creates one.
No non-solicit binding Customer located; Sec 12.3 confirms no no-hire commitment and preserves general recruitment hiring. Likely compliant/absent.

Sec 9.4 gives Customer 30-day convenience termination with prepaid refunds and denies Vendor the same right — favourable. Cross-check Sec 2.1, whose no-termination take-or-pay language may undercut it (address primarily under MINCOMMIT).
Sec 8.2 gives a 30-day opt-out plus a 60-day reminder with deadline extension; Sec 8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice. Likely compliant.
New York law and exclusive New York County courts, no foreign arbitration — within accepted list; likely compliant.
Sec 24.1 permits Customer affiliate/successor assignment without consent; 24.2 restricts Vendor; 24.4 blocks Vendor reaction to our change of control. Likely compliant.

Customer owns Customer Data (14.1) and Deliverables assigned on creation subject to payment (14.2); Vendor retains only Vendor Technology (14.3). Check 15.1 no-model-training limits; likely compliant.

Sec 13.1 grants a Customer-only, non-transferable licence revocable at Vendor's sole discretion excluding Affiliates and contractors — material deviation. Contrast with 13.2/13.3, which grant broader perpetual rights and limit revocation.
Sec 22.1-22.3 limit audits to once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, Vendor-borne cost with a 5% shortfall shift. Likely compliant.

No liquidated damages or penalty payable by Customer identified; the take-or-pay shortfall in Sec 2.1 is the nearest analogue but is better handled under MINCOMMIT. Confirm no early-termination fee elsewhere.

Sec 19.2 limits the Deliverable warranty to 15 days with no correction or refund obligation thereafter — likely below fallback duration. Sec 19.1/19.4 provide an ongoing services warranty and repair/re-perform/refund remedy; assess together.
Sec 18.1 sets CGL, workers' comp, E&O and USD 5M cyber cover with certificates and non-limitation language in 18.2. Likely compliant.

Sec 2.1 imposes USD 2M/year take-or-pay for three years expressly 'without reduction or termination rights' — presence trigger and conflicts with Sec 9.4 convenience termination and Sec 12.3's no-minimum-volume disclaimer.

Sec 11.1 requires immediate cessation of assistance and deletion of Customer Data with no export — material deviation, and directly contradicts 11.2/11.3 (30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion). Cross-check 10.1/10.2 transition period and refunds.
